relevant_passages.quote: Judgment: **no evidence it works, several signs it can't.** (`novamart/jobs/model_train.py`, commit `a1946ff`; registry data.)

Its label is any later status-1 order by the user, with no horizon and no requirement that the purchased product appeared in the recommendation list. Training therefore measures later purchasing propensity more than recommendation-item conversion.

Most importantly, v4 applies only the first coefficient as one scalar multiplier to every nonnegative affinity-v2 pair. The current 948 model-score pairs have zero pair/rank mismatches versus affinity v2 and a nearly constant 0.9755 score ratio; v4 cannot reorder candidates.

Safe recommendation changes should first define an exposure-level outcome with a fixed horizon and recommended-item match, evaluate at user assignment level, remove post-exposure leakage, and make scoring capable of changing rank. The available experiment does not establish material lift. At first intended-v2 exposure per user, any-order conversion within seven days is 3.56% for 19,707 nonrandom users versus 3.40% for 942 random users; recommended-item purchase is 0.27% versus 0%.
